title: Salya against His Nephews
body:
Salya against His Nephews

King Shalya of Madradesa, the maternal uncle of Nakula and Sahadeva, heard that the Pandavas were preparing for war at Upaplavya. He mobilised a massive army, so large that his encampment extended over a length of nearly fifteen miles, and marched to join his nephews. Upon learning of Shalya's movements, Duryodhana devised a sly, calculated plan to intercept him and secure his alliance by trickery.
Duryodhana's officers erected beautifully decorated resthouses at various stages along Shalya's route, lavishing him and his soldiers with sumptuous feasts, drinks, and royal hospitality. Assuming that these extraordinary arrangements had been made by his nephew Yudhishthira, Shalya was deeply moved and called for the attendants to bring King Yudhishthira's consent so that he might reward them. At that moment, Duryodhana stepped forward, revealing himself as the host of the feast.
Stunned but touched by Duryodhana's hospitality and chivalry, Shalya, as a man of honour, asked how he could repay him. Duryodhana immediately demanded that Shalya and his forces fight on the Kaurava side. Bound by the ancient code that eating a host's salt indebted a guest to fulfil their request, Shalya agreed, regretting that he had been tricked into betraying his own nephews.
Shalya proceeded to Upaplavya to meet Yudhishthira and confess his mistake. Yudhishthira, concealing his disappointment, acknowledged the binding nature of Shalya's promise. However, knowing that Shalya was the equal of Krishna in chariot driving, Yudhishthira made a specific request: when Shalya was eventually called upon by Duryodhana to serve as Karna's charioteer during his final duel with Arjuna, Shalya should use his position to dishearten Karna and systematically deflate his pride. Shalya agreed, promising that while he would fight honourably on the Kaurava side to fulfil his vow, he would protect Arjuna's life by undermining Karna's confidence.
